title: Security acceptance flow for Private & Dedicated deployments
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Purpose: Define a concise product acceptance flow, scope, and sign-off checklist that ensures Private and Dedicated deployment offerings meet Redwood's security and compliance bar (SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/HSM) before enabling customer rollouts. Scope: Requirements and acceptance criteria for configuration, surface-level UX for admins, verification steps for SRE/security, CI test hooks, and sign-off owners. Non-goals: Deep cryptographic design (left to ENG research), on-prem installer packaging details beyond integration points, or bespoke customer-specific legal negotiation.

Context: Multiple enterprise prospects have requested explicit pre-sales security attestation. Engineering has landed base SSO/SAML integration (ENG-9102) and an initial RBAC model (ENG-9233) but audit logging and KMS integrations are partially implemented. This PRD clarifies product acceptance boundaries and creates a sign-off checklist to accelerate go/no-go decisions for Private and Dedicated launches.

Primary users: Platform/Customer Admins, Security/Compliance reviewers, Solutions Engineers. Stakeholders: Product (Priya), Security (Ava Martinez), Platform Eng (Liam O'Connor), SRE (Jamal Reed), Solutions Eng (Maya Chen).
requirements_summary: 1) SSO/SAML: Support IdP-initiated SSO, IdP metadata upload, SCIM provisioning optional, clear error surface for misconfig. 2) RBAC: Role templates (Owner/Admin/Operator/ReadOnly), granular model access scopes, audit-able role change history. 3) Audit logging: Immutable audit stream to customer-owned log sink (syslog/HTTPS/S3), guaranteed ordering and retention config, event schema with request/actor/resource/outcome. 4) KMS/HSM: Customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), envelope encryption at rest, key rotation and zero-key fallback mode documented. 5) Admin UX: Secure onboarding flow, permission grant screens, and sign-off modal for enabling production traffic.
acceptance_criteria: SSO/SAML: IdP metadata upload accepts SAML 2.0 metadata files; SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows validated in test tenant; end-to-end login with SAML attributes mapped to RBAC roles; automated test coverage in CI (integration tests) passes.

RBAC: Role templates available in UI and API; policy evaluation unit tests show expected allow/deny for >20 sample scenarios; audit-visible role assignment events (who/when/why) are recorded and exportable.

Audit logs: Events emitted for authentication, authorization decisions, model-inference calls (metadata only), config changes; logs can be streamed to a customer endpoint; retention policy configurable; sampled test log demonstrates correct schema and ingestion into S3/syslog endpoint.

KMS/HSM: Keys can be configured via UI and API; data at rest encrypted with customer-provided KMS; rotation workflow tested with zero-downtime rewrap for active models; fallback to Redwood-managed keys requires explicit admin consent and is audited.

End-to-end: Security team has a reproducible checklist to validate a customer's instance; a signed approval (email/Confluence record) from Security, SRE, and Product is present before GA enablement for an account.
Regression: Automated smoke tests detect regressions for login and basic inference path; SLOs for auth latency (login < 2s median) are measured in staging and marked in the rollout dashboard.
signoff_checklist: Product: PRD reviewed and acceptance criteria declared (Priya Desai)
Security: Threat model reviewed and mitigations validated (Ava Martinez)
Platform Eng: Feature parity tests green and load verified (Liam O'Connor)
SRE: Audit log pipeline validated and alerting configured (Jamal Reed)
Solutions Eng: Customer onboarding guide and runbook published (Maya Chen)
Legal/Compliance: Data handling and key control language approved (Sara Klein)
Release: Release manager cleared deployment checklist and rollback plan (Nikhil Patel)
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: 1) Internal dogfood - configure 2 demo customers in staging and run acceptance checklist. 2) Beta customers by invite (two pilot customers, observe for 3 weeks). 3) GA gated by sign-offs listed above. Rollback: ability to disable customer-provided KMS, revert to managed keys, and revoke SSO sessions; documented in runbook.
test_plan: Automated: CI integration tests for SAML SSO flows, RBAC policy eval harness, audit log emission tests, key rotation smoke. Manual: Security review checklist, penetration test on staging tenant, audit log ingestion into customer sink, manual rotation test with no downtime. Document test artifacts and attach to Confluence page.
open_questions: Do we require SCIM for GA or leave as Beta opt-in? (trade-off: provisioning complexity vs. customer demand)
Acceptable SLA for audit log delivery? Should we provide delivery guarantees or best-effort for customer sinks?
Is HSM integration in scope for GA or planned for a later patch release?
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Initial GA will support SAML and KMS integrations for cloud-managed KMS providers; HSM-specific flows will be documented but delivered in a follow-up release to reduce scope.
Tradeoff: Enabling SCIM by default increases friction for smaller customers; we'll mark SCIM as optional and prioritized for enterprise pilots.
Tradeoff: Audit log delivery will guarantee delivery-to-Rest within our pipeline but rely on customer sink availability; we will surface delivery metrics and retries rather than a hard SLA in GA.
notes: Ensure updated test vectors for RBAC are shared with Eng by 2025-02-20. Coordinate a dry-run call with Security and SRE on 2025-02-27. Customer pilot invites must include the acceptance checklist and runbook link.
